Setup Unable 03 is logged when authentication fails. Either the WPA/WPA2 passphrase was typed wrong or the router's encryption mode is not supported by the printer.

Re-enter the password carefully — it is case sensitive — and confirm the router is using WPA2-PSK (AES).

fixSteps.title: Re-enter password
fixSteps.instruction: Type the Wi-Fi key carefully, mind case and zeros vs Os.

fixSteps.title: Check router mode
fixSteps.instruction: Set router to WPA2-PSK with AES.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: Can I see my password?
faq.a: Check your router's admin page or the label on its base.

title: Setup Unable 04 - DHCP Failed
shortDescription: Printer authenticated but could not obtain an IP address via DHCP.
fullDescription:
After joining the Wi-Fi, the printer asks the router's DHCP server for an IP address. If the server does not respond or the DHCP pool is exhausted, Setup Unable 04 is displayed.

Reboot the router, confirm DHCP is enabled, or assign a static IP via the printer menu.

fixSteps.title: Reboot router
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle the router for 30 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Static IP fallback
fixSteps.instruction: Configure a static IP in Network menu.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.q: Is static IP safe?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you pick an IP outside your DHCP range.

title: Setup Unable 05 - Weak Signal
shortDescription: The Wi-Fi signal level is too low for reliable communication.
fullDescription:
Setup Unable 05 is raised when the printer measures a very low RSSI from the selected access point. Even if authentication succeeds, packet loss is expected to be high.

Move the printer closer, add a Wi-Fi extender, or switch to Ethernet.

fixSteps.title: Relocate printer
fixSteps.instruction: Move the printer nearer to the router.

whenToCallPro: Only for network assessment.

faq.q: What signal is enough?
faq.a: Aim for at least -65 dBm for stable printing.

title: WLAN Setup In Progress
shortDescription: Informational message shown while Wi-Fi is being configured.
fullDescription:
WLAN Setup is an informational display state. It indicates the printer is actively negotiating with the access point (scanning, authenticating, and acquiring an IP).

If the message never clears, the printer is stuck in a setup loop — usually because the access point does not respond. Cancel and rerun setup.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Allow up to 2 minutes for setup to complete.

fixSteps.title: Cancel and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Press Cancel and start wireless setup again.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: How long should setup take?
faq.a: Usually under 30 seconds.

title: Ink Box Near End
shortDescription: The ink absorber pad is almost saturated — plan a replacement soon.
fullDescription:
Brother inkjet MFPs track how much waste ink has been absorbed by an internal pad. At about 90% saturation, 'Ink Box Near End' appears as a warning.

The printer continues to work normally. When it reaches 100%, it will stop and show 'Ink Absorber Full'. Order the replacement pad now to avoid downtime.

fixSteps.title: Order pad
fixSteps.instruction: Order the maintenance kit now.

fixSteps.title: Limit head cleaning
fixSteps.instruction: Avoid unnecessary head cleanings until the pad is replaced.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable resetting the counter.

faq.q: How soon until it stops?
faq.a: Typically a few hundred pages of runway remain.

title: Black Ink Empty
shortDescription: Black ink cartridge is out and must be replaced.
fullDescription:
The black cartridge reports no ink. Brother inkjets cannot print in any mode — including color-only — when black is empty, because all heads share cleaning cycles.

Replace with a genuine Brother LC- cartridge; third-party cartridges may not be recognized.

fixSteps.title: Replace cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new black LC- cartridge.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: Can I print color only?
faq.a: No, Brother blocks printing until black is installed.

title: Color Ink Empty
shortDescription: One of the color cartridges (C/M/Y) is out.
fullDescription:
Replace the exhausted color cartridge. The printer identifies which color is empty on the display. All three color cartridges must have ink for full-color printing to resume.

Mono printing is possible on most Brother models even with color empty, as long as black is still installed.

fixSteps.title: Replace cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Install the indicated color cartridge.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: Can I keep printing mono?
faq.a: Yes, in most Brother models mono printing continues.

title: TN Toner Low
shortDescription: Toner Name (TN) cartridge is running low.
fullDescription:
Brother laser machines flash 'TN Toner Low' when the toner cartridge reaches a threshold (typically 90% used). Printing continues but quality may decline.

Order a replacement TN cartridge. Shake the current cartridge gently to redistribute remaining toner for a few extra pages.

fixSteps.title: Shake cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Rock the cartridge to redistribute toner.

fixSteps.title: Order replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Order the correct TN-xx cartridge for the model.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: How many pages left?
faq.a: Typically 50-200 depending on coverage.

title: DR Drum Life Warning
shortDescription: Drum unit is nearing end of rated life.
fullDescription:
'DR Drum Life' indicates the imaging drum has reached the pagecount for its expected life. The printer will still work, but spots, vertical lines, and ghosting become more likely.

Order the DR-xx drum unit for your model and replace at your convenience. After replacement, reset the drum counter from the menu.

fixSteps.title: Order drum
fixSteps.instruction: Order the correct DR-xx drum unit.

fixSteps.title: Replace and reset
fixSteps.instruction: Install drum and reset the counter via menu.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: Is the drum different from the toner?
faq.a: Yes, on Brother laser models they are separate consumables.

title: Unable to Scan XX
shortDescription: Scanner subsystem encountered an unspecified fault.
fullDescription:
Brother MFPs report 'Unable to Scan XX' when the scan CCD, the scan motor, or the scanner PCB fails to respond. XX is a two-digit subcode logged internally.

If a power cycle does not clear the issue, the scanner unit usually needs service.

fixSteps.title: Unlock scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Check and release the scanner transport lock.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off for 60 seconds and restart.

whenToCallPro: If power cycling and unlocking do not clear the code.

faq.q: Does this stop printing?
faq.a: Printing still works; only scan/copy/fax are blocked.

title: Unable to Align Print Heads
shortDescription: Automatic print head alignment failed on a Brother inkjet.
fullDescription:
'Unable to Align' is shown when the alignment pattern printed during the calibration procedure cannot be read by the scanner or the result is out of range.

Dirty scanner glass, wrong paper size, or a dying ink cartridge all produce this error.

fixSteps.title: Load plain A4
fixSteps.instruction: Use fresh plain A4/Letter for alignment.

fixSteps.title: Clean glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the scanner glass with a lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Retry alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Run the alignment procedure again.

whenToCallPro: If the head still cannot align after cleaning and new ink.

faq.q: Is alignment necessary?
faq.a: Yes, for best color registration on photos.

title: Paper Feed Roller Warning
shortDescription: The paper feed roller is due for replacement.
fullDescription:
Brother tracks the pick roller pagecount. Once it crosses the service interval, the machine warns 'Paper Feed Roller' so you can swap it before misfeeds start.

A feed roller kit (sometimes called PF Kit 1/MP) is available as a user-replaceable part on many models.

fixSteps.title: Order PF Kit
fixSteps.instruction: Order the correct PF kit for your model.

fixSteps.title: Install roller
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the feed roller per the manual.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable opening the cassette housing.

faq.q: How often?
faq.a: Typically every 50,000-100,000 pages.

title: Transfer Roller Service
shortDescription: Transfer roller end-of-life — print quality will decline.
fullDescription:
Brother color laser machines use a transfer roller (or belt) to move toner from the drum to paper. As it wears, voids and halftone banding appear.

Replace the transfer roller per the service manual and reset the counter.

fixSteps.title: Order part
fixSteps.instruction: Order the transfer roller for the model.

fixSteps.title: Install roller
fixSteps.instruction: Install the new transfer roller and reset the counter.

whenToCallPro: For color laser machines under service contract.

faq.q: Will banding go away?
faq.a: Yes, after roller replacement.

title: Print Unable 46 - Waste Ink Full
shortDescription: Waste ink absorber pad is at capacity.
fullDescription: Brother 'Print Unable 46' means the waste ink absorber is full. On inkjet MFCs this is equivalent to 5B00 on Canon or 000070 on Epson.

fixSteps.title: Purge mode reset
fixSteps.instruction: Enter Brother maintenance mode (key sequence varies) and reset purge counter.

fixSteps.title: Pad replacement
fixSteps.instruction: For long-term, physical pad service.

whenToCallPro: Pad replacement is a professional service.

faq.q: Temporary reset?
faq.a: Yes, counter reset gets you going, but physical pad should be replaced soon.

title: Print Unable 50 - Purge Error
shortDescription: Purge unit failed to complete cleaning cycle.
fullDescription: Brother 'Print Unable 50' indicates a purge unit fault — pump jam, wiper stuck, or cap station fault.

fixSteps.title: Clean wiper
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and clean wiper blade with distilled water.

fixSteps.title: Retest
fixSteps.instruction: Power on and try head cleaning.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, purge unit replacement.

whenToCallPro: Purge unit replacement is professional.

faq.q: Why does purge fail?
faq.a: Dried ink or debris — regular printing prevents this.

title: Print Unable 0A - Head Thermistor
shortDescription: Printhead temperature sensor fault.
fullDescription: Brother 'Print Unable 0A' indicates the printhead thermistor is reporting out-of-range temperature, preventing safe printing.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60s.

fixSteps.title: Reseat head cable
fixSteps.instruction: If accessible, reseat printhead cable.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Replace printhead if sensor failed.

whenToCallPro: Printhead replacement is professional.

faq.q: Safe to keep trying?
faq.a: No — thermistor fault could cause damage if ignored.

title: Print Unable 02 Variant - Head Drive
shortDescription: Printhead drive circuit error variant.
fullDescription: A variant of 'Print Unable 02' seen on newer Brother firmware — head drive circuit reported overcurrent or underdrive.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off 60s.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Update Brother firmware.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Mainboard or printhead replacement.

whenToCallPro: Board-level service.

faq.q: Firmware first?
faq.a: Yes — some variants are cleared by update.

title: Replace Lower Tray Kit
shortDescription: Lower tray (LT) feed kit reached service life.
fullDescription: Brother 'Replace LT Kit' appears on models with optional lower tray (LT) cassettes — its rollers need replacement.

fixSteps.title: Order kit
fixSteps.instruction: Order the correct LT kit for your model.

fixSteps.title: Swap rollers
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cassette, replace rollers per instructions.

fixSteps.title: Reset counter
fixSteps.instruction: Reset LT counter via service menu.

whenToCallPro: Uncomfortable users may prefer a technician.

faq.q: How often?
faq.a: Typically 100,000+ pages.

title: Unable to Clean - Head Cleaning Failed
shortDescription: Head cleaning cycle could not be completed.
fullDescription: Brother 'Unable to Clean' occurs when the printhead cleaning cycle does not finish — usually ink starvation, purge fault, or dry head.

fixSteps.title: Check ink
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure cartridges have ink; replace if low.

fixSteps.title: Deep clean
fixSteps.instruction: Run multiple deep cleaning cycles if option available.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: If head is dry beyond recovery, replace printhead.

whenToCallPro: Printhead replacement is professional.

faq.q: Prevention?
faq.a: Print at least weekly to keep ink flowing.

title: Unable to Init - Startup Failure
shortDescription: Printer failed to complete startup initialization.
fullDescription: Brother 'Unable to Init' means the printer could not complete self-check on startup — related to sensors, carriage, or firmware.

fixSteps.title: Check obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Open covers and remove any packaging or debris.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 60s.

fixSteps.title: Firmware recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Connect USB and use Brother firmware recovery tool.

whenToCallPro: Hardware failure needs technician.

faq.q: Same as Init Unable?
faq.a: Similar — Brother uses both names across models.

title: Machine Error E5 - Engine Error
shortDescription: Brother engine/formatter general fault.
fullDescription: Brother 'Machine Error E5' is a general engine error — communication lost between mainboard and engine controller or unrecoverable exception.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 60s.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest firmware.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Mainboard or engine replacement.

whenToCallPro: Board-level service.

faq.q: Is data lost?
faq.a: Settings are usually preserved across a reset.

title: Machine Error E6 - Fuser/Heater Fault
shortDescription: Brother fuser heater fault.
fullDescription: Brother 'Machine Error E6' specifically indicates a fuser heater failure on laser models — similar to HP 50.x and Canon #851.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat fuser connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Replace fuser assembly.

whenToCallPro: Fuser work is professional.

faq.q: Safe to retry?
faq.a: No — stop until fuser is fixed.

title: Fax Can't Send - Transmission Failure
shortDescription: Fax transmission failed.
fullDescription: Brother 'Can't Send' (fax error) indicates the fax could not transmit — line issue, busy, or protocol fault.

fixSteps.title: Retry
fixSteps.instruction: Try sending again later.

fixSteps.title: Check line
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure phone line works with a normal phone.

fixSteps.title: Adjust settings
fixSteps.instruction: Lower fax speed (ECM disabled or reduced speed) for noisy/VoIP lines.

whenToCallPro: Rarely.

faq.q: Does VoIP cause issues?
faq.a: Yes — fax over VoIP often needs lower speeds or T.38.

title: Fax Can't Receive - Reception Failure
shortDescription: Incoming fax could not be received.
fullDescription: Brother 'Can't Receive' occurs when an incoming fax fails — often due to line issues, out of paper, or memory full.

fixSteps.title: Load paper
fixSteps.instruction: Add paper to tray.

fixSteps.title: Clear memory
fixSteps.instruction: Print or delete stored faxes.
